arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Katze argued that the issue is whether DWI is a violent felony for sentencing.
Ms. Kruger stated that drunk driving endangers lives by its very nature.
Justice Breyer compared burglary and drunk driving to test the risk standard.
Justice Ginsburg noted that all listed crimes present a serious risk of injury.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks if a drunk driving offense fits the legal definition of a violent felony. This classification changes the possible prison sentence for the defendant.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on January 15, 2008.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the court to reject the violent felony label for drunk driving.
The government wants the court to accept the violent felony label for drunk driving.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that drunk driving lacks the specific intent to harm required for a violent felony.
The government argues that drunk driving inherently creates a serious risk of physical injury to others.

Chief Justice Roberts questioned whether the legal canon of ejusdem generis applies to the statute.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome determines the statutory sentencing range for defendants with prior drunk driving convictions. It defines the scope of the Armed Career Criminal Act. It impacts how courts classify offenses involving risk rather than intent.
